source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's NVA5-NVA7 campus in Sterling, Virginia publishes 116 MW of IT capacity, the third largest figure of any mapped Virginia facility and about 4.5 percent of the state's 2,563.4 MW of published capacity.

The more telling number is the gap between the 376 Virginia facilities mapped and the 29 that publish a megawatt figure. Most of the state's data center footprint is invisible at the power level, and this campus is one of the few that is not. Published capacity is a measure of electrical provisioning, which is the constraint that matters for AI, not of how much compute is actually installed or run.

The 116 MW is a capacity figure, not consumption. The operator publishes no rack count, accelerator count, or power usage effectiveness on the spec page read here, so any translation to racks requires an outside assumption: at 40 kW per rack, roughly 2,900 racks, at 10 kW per rack, roughly 11,600. Neither is CyrusOne's claim, and the split between AI training and traditional colocation at this site is not published.

The certifications field is empty, which limits what can be said about standards this campus has been qualified against, and the address and postal code are unpublished, so it can be placed in Sterling and no more precisely. The case for this campus mattering to AI rests on the 116 MW and its rank, both published, and on the rack-level composition, which is not.
